what_breaks: A transfer order is holding a reservation it never released. required_quantity stays raised, so that stock stops being sellable to customers with no error anywhere. This is the defining failure mode of the module.
runbook: Take transferOrderIds from $.meta.transferOrderIds. Decide per TO whether Zoho actually moved the stock (GET /transferorders/:id on Zoho), then let POST /transfer-orders/cron/reconcile do the release. DO NOT hand-edit required_quantity - the Zoho-pull cron and both ledgers write that row.
notes: metricValue = $.meta.count. Threshold in code is 48h (TRANSFER_ORDER_STUCK_RESERVATION_HOURS), so anything reported here is already two days stale. PREREQUISITE: this only fires if something calls POST /transfer-orders/cron/stuck-reservations - see to-reconcile-cron rows. Drift query is in the wiki gotchas page.

what_breaks: At least one reservation has been held over 48h
runbook: Usually one TO parked at PICKING_ISSUE_RAISED (status 8) waiting on a TL, which legitimately holds its reservation. Confirm before escalating.
notes: Expect a real floor from status-8 TOs. If that floor is persistent, split the detector by status rather than raising the threshold - a genuinely lost release and a TO awaiting a TL look identical here.

flow: Zoho draft failed - TO holds stock and cannot be picked
what_breaks: createTransferOrder swallows the Zoho failure (.catch(() => false)) and returns 201 with zohoSynced:false. The TO exists, the stock IS reserved, and it is NOT pickable because the picking query requires a Zoho id. It sits holding stock until someone notices.
runbook: POST /transfer-orders/:id/retry-zoho per affected TO. Read meta.zohoCreateError for the cause. If Zoho itself is down expect the zoho SO alerts to be firing too.
notes: THE API RETURNS 201 ON THIS PATH - no HTTP-level alert will ever catch it, only this TraceCode. Note the same code is also emitted by getZohoTransferOrder and updateZohoTransferOrder in zoho.api.service.ts (:824/:853/:898), so it covers three different calls - check the call site before assuming it is a draft failure.

flow: Zoho draft failed - TO holds stock and cannot be picked
what_breaks: A transfer order failed to sync to Zoho and is unpickable
runbook: Same retry-zoho path. Single occurrence is worth a look because the caller was told the TO succeeded.
notes: Fires on one occurrence deliberately: the failure is invisible to the user who created the TO, so nobody else will report it.

flow: Send-to-transit failing - the point of no return
what_breaks: Dispatch is failing partway through a 7-step sequence that spans two Zoho round trips. A partial completion leaves batches deactivated or reservations released without the status advancing - or the reverse.
runbook: Check Zoho state for the TO before retrying - a lost response means Zoho already moved it. TRANSFER_ORDER_ALREADY_IN_TRANSIT_ON_ZOHO in the same window means the reconcile path handled it. Do not re-dispatch blind.
notes: Guarded by TRANSFER_ORDER_IN_TRANSIT_LOCK with a 120s TTL because of the two Zoho calls. Recovery is the reconcile cron's resume-in-transit stage, so this alert and to-reconcile-cron are paired - if reconcile is not running, nothing self-heals.

flow: Send-to-transit failing - the point of no return
runbook: Check whether the TO is sitting at PHARMACIST_ACCEPTED (status 15) older than 15 min - that is the reconcile cron's stuck-pre-transit case.
notes: assertReadyForTransit re-checks picked==requested at dispatch, so a legitimate rejection (pharmacist changed batches) also lands here. Read error_message before treating as an incident.

what_breaks: The module's only self-healing mechanism is dead. Lost-response dispatches never resume, invoices are never discovered, and the stuck-reservation alarm never fires - so every other alert in this sheet degrades silently with it.
runbook: Check cron-job.org for POST /transfer-orders/cron/reconcile and POST /transfer-orders/cron/stuck-reservations. Both are RetoolAuth routes on the cron controller.
notes: VERIFY FIRST: neither TO cron endpoint appears in the wiki cron inventory (captured 2026-08-12, TO work continued to 08-18) - they may never have been scheduled. If so, schedule them BEFORE building any other row here, because to-stuck-reservation depends entirely on the stuck-reservations job running. Set treatMissingData=breaching.

what_breaks: The reconcile cron is running but erroring on individual transfer orders
runbook: $.meta.stage tells you which half failed - 'resume-in-transit' or 'discover-invoice'. Invoice-discovery errors are lower stakes than resume failures.
notes: Per-TO try/catch means one bad TO does not stop the sweep, but it also means a permanently broken TO errors every single run - watch for the same transferOrderId repeating rather than raw count.

what_breaks: Transfer orders are being created but never claimed. Picker eligibility is a Redis-only gate that FAILS CLOSED: an unset or malformed TRANSFER_ORDER_PICKER_USER_IDS key means nobody is eligible and TOs never enter any picker queue, silently.
runbook: Check the TRANSFER_ORDER_PICKER_USER_IDS Redis key exists, is valid JSON, and is env-prefixed. Utils.safeJsonParse falls back to [] on malformed input - which means zero eligible pickers, not all pickers.
notes: No TraceCode exists for 'eligibility list empty' - this is inferred from the absence of claims, which is why it needs a composite alarm and a long window. Worth adding a log line when the parsed list is empty; that would replace this whole row with a direct signal.

what_breaks: Transfer orders are queuing longer than expected before being claimed
runbook: Normal if warehouse staffing is thin - confirm with the warehouse before treating as a bug.
notes: A TO loses to every SDD/NDD customer order for its first 24h by design, so slow claiming is expected and this row will have a real floor. Baseline before setting the ratio.
